Raj (ACME-POC): Hey team — POC with ACME. We're not seeing trace correlation in Redwood Console; requests show up but trace_id is null. Any config I'm missing?
Mike (platform): Do you set x-redwood-trace-id? We prefer that header for span correlation. x-request-id is passthrough but not used for trace spans. Can you paste an example request?
Raj (ACME-POC): curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'x-request-id: 12345' 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' — returns 200 but console shows no trace.
Jess (sales-eng): Looping Angela + Mike. Customer is picky about logs/exporting.
Mike (platform): Try: curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'x-redwood-trace-id: 0xabc123def' 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' — our runtime will attach that to spans. Also check you aren't stripping headers in a proxy.
Raj (ACME-POC): Switched to x-redwood-trace-id — traces now appear in Console. Progress.
Raj (ACME-POC): However Splunk drain doesn't show trace_id in logs. We're using the log drain configured in the Project -> Exports page.
Mike (platform): Two things: 1) confirm "include_trace_in_logs" is enabled on the route/export config; 2) check log exporter transform mode (nested vs flat). We send structured JSON with top-level "trace_id" when include_trace is on.
Raj (ACME-POC): Where's that setting? I only saw a toggle in Console under Observability -> Exports.
Mike (platform): Console path: Project > Routes > <route> > Exports. Toggle "Include trace_id in log payload". For terraform you can set route_export { include_trace = true }.
Jess (sales-eng): Customer asks about PII and raw log export. Angela?
Angela (security): By default we redact sensitive fields for hosted drains. If customer needs raw logs to send to their SIEM, we require a DPA + dedicated drain (or Dedicated/Private deployment). Also need to answer Q12 in the security questionnaire about retention and redaction.
Raj (ACME-POC): We're also seeing 429s when exporting large embedding batches during the POC. Backoff recommended?
Mike (platform): Use batching size ~100 for embeddings and exponential backoff on 429. Also for POC we can route traffic to a dedicated temporary pool to avoid tenant throttles — that reduces 429s.
Raj (ACME-POC): One more oddity: trace sampling looks very low. Only a handful of traces forwarded.
Mike (platform): Sample rate defaults to 1% for high-volume routes. You can override per-route in Console: Observability > Tracing > Sampling override. You can also force a sample by sending header `x-trace-sampled: 1`.
Raj (ACME-POC): Increased sampling to 10% and I'm seeing more traces. Splunk still not showing trace_id though — looks like Splunk's ingest pipeline isn't extracting the field.
Mike (platform): If Splunk uses field-extraction regex, nested JSON can be missed. Recommend setting the log_exporter.transform = "flat" so trace_id is a top-level string, or update Splunk props/transforms to parse JSON.
Raj (ACME-POC): Got it. I'll change transform and re-ingest a few test logs.
Jess (sales-eng): I'll open a support ticket to request a temporary dedicated pool and ask eng-exports to sanity-check Splunk parsing.
Jess (sales-eng): Creating ticket now.
OpsBot: Ticket SUP-8921 created: "POC ACME — dedicated pool + Splunk field extraction help" assigned to eng-exports.
Raj (ACME-POC): Thanks everyone — much better. Will follow up after re-ingest. :thumbsup:
Mike (platform): If you hit any more blockers ping me; I can jump into the Splunk parsing with sample payloads.
Angela (security): Also send the signed DPA request if they want raw logs; security will triage.
Raj (ACME-POC): Will do.
